decisive_items: Initial histopathologic findings showed a Breslow thickness of 6 mm, 14 mitotic figures/mm2
Cross section of nerve showing malignant cells with mitotic activity, effacing residual nerve axons, disrupted neuronal cells, and peritumoral and intratumoral lymphocytes
recurring forehead lesion, first excised 6 years prior to presentation
response.rationale: Frontal nerve biopsy confirms malignant melanoma, and the history of recurrent melanoma with perineural invasion explains the orbital and cavernous sinus findings as secondary spread rather than a separate syndrome.

rejected.why: Orbital apex syndrome is an anatomic syndrome that incompletely fits because optic nerve function is preserved; it is a downstream manifestation of the melanoma, not the underlying diagnosis.
Cavernous sinus syndrome describes the MRI-observed extension of the mass, but the biopsy-proven malignant melanoma is the definitive and most likely diagnosis.
